title: Initiality of generic base change on pointed etale neighbourhoods
statement: Let $D$ be an integral scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme], $K=k(D)$ and $\eta:\operatorname{Spec}K\to D$ [def-sc-function-field]. For an algebraically closed field $\Omega$ and geometric point $s:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ [def-weil-geometric-point], the functor between categories of pointed etale neighbourhoods [def-weil-pbc-etale-site] sending $(V,v)$ at $s\circ\eta$ to $(V\times_D\operatorname{Spec}K,(v,s))$ at $s$ is initial.

source.place: Tags 02GH, 01ZM, 07RP; generic counit argument of blueprint lem-sc-affine-generic-second, proof paragraph 3

proof.text: The extension theorem gives a morphism from a base-changed pointed neighbourhood to every pointed neighbourhood over K.

For two pointed maps sigma,sigma-prime from V_K to W, their agreement locus E is open because W -> Spec K is unramified. It contains the marking. The morphism eta is a preimmersion (Mathlib Scheme.fromSpecStalk isPreimmersion), and so is V_K -> V. An inducing map pulls back some open V0 to E. The marking v factors through V0. Base change of V0 -> V lands inside E, so it equalizes sigma and sigma-prime; the marking and all morphisms are retained. This is proved in the private helper exists_map_comp_eq_generic_baseChangeNbhd using FormallyUnramified.eqLocus and IsOpenImmersion.lift.
The categories of pointed etale neighbourhoods are cofiltered. Apply Functor.initial_of_exists_of_isCofiltered with the extension and equalization criteria.
